annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The workspace overview: a zoomed-out, per-monitor view of every workspace. The daemon is the layout authority (engines are the only source of where a non-current workspace's windows belong) and publishes a per-(screen, desktop) model while the overview is open; the KWin overview effect renders it and sends every mutation back as a verb. Verbs are fire-and-forget: every refusal is a debug log and no state change, and the effect learns the outcome from the next overviewModelChanged. Screen ids are the daemon's canonical physical ids; window ids are the daemon's composite window ids; desktop ids are KWin UUID strings as workspaceMap reports them.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Streaming gate. The effect calls this with true BEFORE its first overviewModel() replay; while closed overviewModel() answers an empty string and overviewModelChanged never fires. Opening also suppresses the workspace OSD hints (snap-back, displaced) until closed. The daemon watches the caller's unique bus name and resets to closed when it vanishes, so a crashed effect cannot leave the model streaming. Only the caller that opened may close; a close from any other name is ignored.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Replay half of overviewModelChanged. Empty while closed, while the workspaces feature is off, or before adoption.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Versioned JSON object, v 1: {v, generation, workspaceMapGeneration, activity, screens: {screenId: {logicalSize: {w, h}, workspaces: {desktopId: {sliceIndex, index, name, current, mode, windows: [{id, rect: {x, y, w, h}, floating, minimized, sticky, column, tile}], strip?: {viewOffset, columns: [{rect, tabbed, activeTab, tiles: [{id, rect}]}]}}}}}}. Rects are workspace-local logical pixels (relative to the output's logical geometry origin), integers, unzoomed; a null rect (all zeros) means the daemon has no geometry for that entry. sliceIndex is the workspace's position in its screen's slice (JSON objects do not preserve order), index its live 1-based global desktop number, name its declared name or empty, current whether it is the screen's current workspace. mode is one of snapping, tiling, scrolling, none. The windows array is unordered; the effect sorts by stacking order. strip is present only for scrolling workspaces: its column and tile rects already include the view offset (a parked column lies outside the workspace), and viewOffset is the strip's viewport position for the pan verb. generation orders model payloads (a receiver drops non-increasing values); workspaceMapGeneration names the workspaceMap generation the model was built against and a receiver holding a different map must re-request workspaceMap() and then overviewModel(). Both counters restart with the daemon's service name.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The model changed while the overview is open. Change-gated (only a real payload difference fires) and coalesced to one emission per event-loop turn. Never fires while closed.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The daemon's view of the open state changed (the setOverviewOpen gate, a watcher reset, or a feature teardown).

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The overview toggle shortcut fired daemon-side. The effect toggles its state; the toggle is a no-op there when another fullscreen effect holds the slot or the keyboard grab fails, and the effect reports the actual outcome through setOverviewOpen.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The daemon asks the effect to close the overview without changing focus: the workspaces feature is being torn down, the current activity changed, or the daemon is exiting.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: The effect reports whether its toggle actually started or stopped the overview. A report of false while the daemon considers the overview open closes the gate the same way setOverviewOpen(false) would.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Switch one screen to one of its own workspaces by desktop id. Refused when the desktop is not in that screen's slice. Deferred behind the reconciler's ledger like the delta verbs.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Move a window to an existing workspace, handing it to the target context's placement engine through the cross-mode handoff with a drop intent. dropX/dropY are workspace-local logical pixels, unzoomed. In a scrolling target the drop point decides new column versus join column (stacked or tabbed); in a snapping target it decides the zone (no zone leaves the window free at its live frame); in a tiling target it decides the insert slot. Refused for sticky windows, unknown windows, and desktops not owned by the named screen. A window floating in the source arrives non-floating in the target; the overview never carries a float bit.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Move a window into a NEW workspace on a screen. sliceIndex is the 0-based gap index (0 = above the first workspace, sliceSize = below the trailing empty one). A gap at or past the trailing empty workspace reuses that workspace instead of inserting (niri's rule); a smaller index inserts a workspace there, reserved against the destroy debounce until the window arrives. dropX/dropY as in moveWindowToWorkspace; a new scrolling workspace always receives the window as its first column.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Move a workspace to a new 0-based position inside its own screen's slice. A named workspace also rewrites its declaration position so the next re-apply agrees. Refused when the desktop is not owned by the screen or the index is out of range.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Re-own a workspace to another screen at a 0-based slice index, windows riding along. Refused when the source slice would drop to zero, when the target screen is unknown to the map, or when the desktop is unowned. A pinned workspace rewrites its declaration output.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Rename a workspace. Capped at the workspace name length limit. A named workspace rewrites its declaration; a dynamic one pushes the name to KWin through the reconciler's name ledger.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Pin (declare as a named workspace, so it survives being emptied) or unpin (remove the declaration) a workspace. Pinning appends a Workspaces.Named declaration built from the workspace's current KWin name (or a generated one), its owner screen and its slice index; unpinning removes the declaration whose name the workspace carries. Both go through the daemon's settings so the declaration list stays the single source of truth.

annotation.name: org.gtk.GDBus.DocString
annotation.value: Pan a scrolling workspace's strip by a pixel delta along the strip. The screen's current workspace pans live; any other workspace pans its stored view, which shows the next time that workspace is focused. Ignored for non-scrolling workspaces.
